offers_products.reason: Main offering is baseball games and entertainment; merchandise is incidental to the team and Battery real estate.

offers_services.reason: Sells live baseball entertainment, tickets, media rights and sponsorships, plus leasing Battery Atlanta retail, office and residential space.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Fans buy tickets, concessions and merchandise; Battery Atlanta residents rent apartments and shoppers visit.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Corporate sponsors, broadcasters and Battery office and retail tenants like Comcast, Papa John's and Home Depot.

recurring_revenue.reason: Revenue is mostly per-game tickets, concessions and sponsorship, though media rights and leases recur; mixed, leaning one-off.

cyclical_demand.reason: Tickets, premium seating, sponsorships and discretionary entertainment spending can be cut in a downturn.

big_ticket.reason: Game tickets, concessions and merchandise are small, frequent purchases; leases are ongoing rent.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for the stadium experience, brand, media rights and leased property, not mainly staff time.

large_customers.reason: Main buyers are fans and households; sponsors and tenants are a smaller part of revenue.

asset_heavy.reason: Owns Truist Park operations, spring training complex and Battery Atlanta mixed-use properties needing ongoing development investment.

notes: Mix of baseball team and Battery real estate; recurring revenue is a judgment call.
